title: Zero Axial Loading Training Protocol
author: Derek D.
desc:
Universal Rules
"Blow Before You Go": Exhale gently just before and during the hardest part of every rep. Never hold breath and brace.
Left Knee Stop Signal: If left knee buckles or surge of shin stiffness/drop foot, end set immediately.
Left Hand Check: If grip feels weak, switch to wrist straps or reduce load. Do not force fingers 3-5.
Cervical Neutral: Keep neck packed (slight double chin, ears over shoulders). If shooting pain, tingling, or increased left hand weakness: stop.

ex.note: TRS Diaphragmatic Breathing: 3 min lying on back, knees bent. 4-second inhale expanding belly and pelvic floor, 6-second exhale letting it sink.
Cat-Cow: 10 slow, gentle cycles to introduce fluid mobility to the lumbar spine.
Standing Glute Activation: Squeeze glutes hard for 5 seconds × 5 reps. This neurologically inhibits the hypertonic pelvic floor.
Ankle Circles with Toe Lifts: 10 circles each direction per ankle, then 10 toe lifts (targets drop-foot neural pathway).
Shoulder Rotations: 10 slow, controlled circles each direction. Keep mid-range, no aggressive end-range during cervical phase.

Tibialis Wall-Lean Hold: 45-60s (upper back on wall, feet 12" out, pull toes up)

Single-Leg Quad/Glute Iso-Switch: 30s standing on left leg, 5-degree knee bend, max-squeeze quad and glute
light KB at chest, sit to box, right hand on wall/rack
45° incline, chest down, wrist straps if needed
Standing Pallof Press: 3×12/side (band at chest height, anti-rotation)
slow eccentric on left side
Single-Leg Glute Bridges: 2×10/side (drive through left heel)
Lie on your back with knees bent over a pillow. Focus on deep, silent nasal inhales that gently expand your lower abdomen and drop your pelvic floor. This is the deliberate opposite of bracing.
Hills or treadmill incline. Maintain 50/50 weight distribution between legs. Every 10 min: stop for 5 slow belly breaths, pelvic floor dropping on inhale.

slow, rhythmic reps. Extend your left arm out to a "waiter's tray" position with fingers pointing down while simultaneously tilting your right ear to your right shoulder. Return to center. Move gently
